A NOTE TO YOUR FILM ↓
01 / A Note to Your Film
Who is watching
whom?

Dear Director and Producer,

Chris spends the night guarding a closet. Susan spends it guarding him. What stays with me is the reversal at the center of the film: the monster stops moving, and the fear quietly shifts onto his mother. That turn is what makes the story linger.

In the edit, I’d want to protect that shift — from external terror to intimate unease — while holding onto the love that keeps the two of them together.

03 / A Little About Me

Editor by craft.
Story lover
by nature.

I’m Ada Qiyue Wu, an MFA filmmaker at the USC School of Cinematic Arts. I come to the editing room with a director’s curiosity, an editor’s patience, and a genuine affection for emotional detail.

Editing has been the thread running through my film education and practice. I began in the inaugural Editing Director cohort at the Communication University of Zhejiang and kept developing my craft through shorts, documentaries, and feature-film post-production. Before coming to USC, I received formal offers from the film editing programs at AFI Conservatory and Chapman University. In my MFA training, I study with Duwayne Dunham, and my mentor is Bartholomew Burcham.

What I love most about editing is finding the most sincere feeling inside a story and shaping the clearest, strongest version of it on screen.

AVID MEDIA COMPOSER PREMIERE PRO DAVINCI RESOLVE SOUND & VFX
